title: Phase 6L Bidirectional Sensitivity Analysis
description: Offline rescoring of saved generation outputs under bidirectional parent/subtechnique credit

ranking_stability.cti-ate: LLM-only and E0' swap ranks 1 and 2; D1 remains superior to HD

limitation_paragraph: Sensitivity Analysis Findings (CRIT-02 Remediation): The standard headline generation metric (f1_sub) enforces directional credit where only predicted subtechniques credit parent ground truth targets. Under this rule, because the generation prompt instructed the model to 'exclude any subtechnique IDs', the model was penalized on CTI-ATTACK where 47.8% of ground truth targets are subtechniques. Offline rescoring with bidirectional parent/subtechnique credit awards credit symmetrically when parent technique predictions match subtechnique targets. Under bidirectional credit, all arm scores on CTI-ATTACK increase by +0.1506 to +0.1870, but the relative arm rankings DO NOT CHANGE: LLM-only (0.5834) > D1 (0.5249) > HD (0.4566) > E0' (0.3960). On cti-ate (where 0% of ground truth targets are subtechniques), scores increase moderately (+0.0521 to +0.0860), with LLM-only slightly edging E0' (0.5494 vs 0.5313), while D1 remains superior to HD (0.5144 vs 0.4554). Conclusion: The prompt-metric contradiction depressed the absolute score baseline on CTI-ATTACK but did not alter the substantive experimental conclusions regarding RAG vs LLM-only performance or budget expansion gains.
